en.name: Basil, dried
en.summary: Dried basil keeps 12 months in a cool, dark cupboard. That figure is a flavour window rather than a safety limit — dried herbs do not spoil, they fade, and an eighteen-month-old jar of basil is weak rather than dangerous.
en.pantry: 12 months in an airtight jar, cool, dark and away from the hob. There is not enough water in a dried leaf for anything to grow in it, so the clock is measuring aroma: the volatile oils that make basil smell of basil escape steadily, faster in heat and light, and what is left eventually tastes of green dust. Test rather than trusting the date — open the jar and smell it, then crush a pinch between your fingers and smell again. If warming it in your hand releases nothing, it has nothing left to give a dish.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for dried basil, and the fridge is the wrong place for it. Dried herbs are hygroscopic, so a cold jar opened in a warm kitchen collects condensation, and damp dried basil clumps and can then genuinely mould. A sealed jar in a cool cupboard is what the published figure assumes.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published either. Freezing would slow the aroma loss, but the same condensation problem applies every time the jar comes out, and a 12-month figure on something you use a teaspoon of at a time is not the constraint people imagine. If you want basil that tastes of basil in winter, freeze fresh leaves in oil instead — dried basil and fresh basil are not really the same ingredient.
en.thawing: Not applicable — dried basil is a cupboard spice and should not be frozen.
spoilage: No smell at all when you crush a pinch — the aroma has gone.
A dull grey-green colour where the leaf was bright.
Clumping, which means moisture has got into the jar.
Mould or a musty smell in a jar that got damp, the only real safety issue here.
tips: Buy small jars; you are buying aroma, and aroma does not keep.
Crush a pinch in your palm before using — it wakes the oils up.
Add dried basil early in cooking and fresh basil at the very end.
Never shake it straight from the jar over a steaming pan; the steam gets in.

faq.q: How long does dried basil last?
faq.a: 12 months in an airtight jar in a cool, dark cupboard.
No. Dried herbs fade rather than spoil. An old jar is weak, not unsafe — only a damp jar that has grown mould should be thrown out.

faq.q: How can you tell if dried basil is still good?
faq.a: Crush a pinch between your fingers and smell it. If nothing comes up, it will not do anything for your food either.

zh.name: 乾燥羅勒
zh.summary: 乾燥羅勒放在陰涼避光的櫥櫃可放 12 個月。這個數字是風味的窗口，不是安全的上限——乾燥香草不會腐敗，它是「淡掉」；一罐放了一年半的羅勒是味道弱，不是危險。
zh.pantry: 氣密罐、陰涼、避光、遠離爐台，12 個月。乾燥葉片裡的水分不足以讓任何東西生長，所以這個時鐘量的是香氣：讓羅勒聞起來像羅勒的那些揮發性精油會持續逃走，在高溫與光線下跑得更快，最後剩下的只是綠色的粉塵味。請用測試取代看日期——打開罐子聞一下，再用手指捏碎一小撮、再聞一次。如果在手心搓熱都放不出香氣，它對一道菜也沒什麼可以貢獻了。
zh.fridge: 乾燥羅勒沒有公布的冷藏期限，而冰箱是錯的地方。乾燥香草會吸濕，冰過的罐子在溫暖廚房打開就會結露，而受潮的乾羅勒會結塊，接著才真的可能發霉。公布的數字預設的條件，是密封罐放在陰涼櫥櫃裡。
zh.freezer: 冷凍同樣沒有期限數據。冷凍確實會拖慢香氣流失，但每次拿出來一樣有結露問題；而且對一種每次只用一小匙的東西來說，12 個月並不是大家想像中的那種限制。想在冬天吃到真的有羅勒味的羅勒，請改成把新鮮葉子泡油冷凍——乾羅勒和新鮮羅勒根本不算同一種材料。
zh.thawing: 不適用——乾燥羅勒是櫥櫃香料，不應冷凍。
spoilage: 捏碎一小撮完全聞不到味道——香氣已經走了。
顏色從鮮綠變成暗沉的灰綠。
結塊，代表水氣跑進罐子了。
受潮的罐子長霉或有霉味——這是這裡唯一真正的安全問題。
tips: 買小罐；你買的是香氣，而香氣不耐放。
使用前在手心捏碎搓一下，可以把精油喚醒。
乾燥羅勒早點下鍋，新鮮羅勒最後才放。
不要直接在冒蒸氣的鍋子上方抖罐子，蒸氣會跑進去。

faq.a: 氣密罐放陰涼避光的櫥櫃，12 個月。

faq.q: 放很久的乾燥羅勒有危險嗎？
faq.a: 沒有。乾燥香草是淡掉而不是腐敗。舊罐子只是味道弱；只有受潮長霉的才該丟。

faq.q: 怎麼判斷乾燥羅勒還能不能用？
faq.a: 用手指捏碎一小撮聞聞看。如果什麼都聞不到，它對你的菜也不會有任何作用。
